correctness.rationale: For n≥4, distinct destinations after 0–3 forward jumps give complete exact polynomial entries. T2 diagonal is positive and one-hop entry is a h[1-(a+b)h/2], yielding H2=2/A. T3 diagonal q3(ah) decreases strictly to and past a unique positive root rho; its one-hop quadratic is everywhere positive (strict negative discriminant), two-hop entries are a b h²[3-(a+b+c)h]/6, and three-hop entries are positive. Therefore H3=min(rho/M,3/C) with necessity, sufficiency and nonreentry for every positive rate vector. M<A<C<2A gives 3/4<H3/H2<3/2. Two explicit strictly positive 4-cycle families approach both bounds, and a one-site defect produces one exact strict order switch R=rho/(2-rho). Standalone rational checker produced 52,032 exact matrix-entry and 7,488 exact row-sum comparisons, and 2,240 supplementary two-sided horizon checks. Numeric experiments are not used to prove the infinite parameter claim.

originality.rationale: No equivalent two-polynomial, sharp all-positive-rate directed-cycle frontier was found in accessible same-object results or the primary literature inspected. The nearest published heterogeneous-cycle classification covers RK4 with different polynomial obstructions and n≥5, not the RK2-vs-RK3 ratio or n=4. A second publication establishes an order-three reversal for symmetric complete multipartite graph Laplacians but not variable-rate directed cycles. Established positive-RK theories describe general sufficient/strict class thresholds rather than this exact joint comparison. Historical priority remains provisional, and a failed text search is not independent proof of originality.
residual_risks: Other historical specialist papers may have an equivalent result under different words or an unindexed representation; the search is bounded.
The finding concerns only the completed-step polynomial on autonomous directed cycles with at least four states; no internal stage or arbitrary generator classification.

value.rationale: For positivity-constrained Markov dynamics, the largest admissible step is a natural and nontrivial integrator-choice invariant. The theorem gives all-rate, all-cycle-length exact endpoints for both polynomial orders, nonreentry, a strict sharp 25% loss/50% gain range, and a naturally motivated one-rate defect transition. These are structural rather than renaming or arbitrary finite samples and directly support timestep/method selection. Accuracy, cost and nonlinearity are explicitly excluded.
